_description: LLM provider defaults. popular_models drives the ordered global selector and offline fallback independently of token constraints. POLICY (2026-07-23): popular_models lists only models with >= 1M-token context windows — providers whose models are all below 1M carry an empty list and contribute nothing to the global selector (their models stay reachable via the live per-provider fetch_models dropdown). base_url directly configures the nine OpenAI-compatible native providers; dedicated OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini providers use SDK defaults, while OpenRouter has its own gateway default. Runtime proxy credentials can override supported endpoints. Model specs are enriched by model_registry.json (OpenRouter cache).

agent._description: Agent execution defaults. recursion_limit and compaction.ratio are sourced from the environment (AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT, COMPACTION_RATIO via core.config.Settings) — these JSON values are last-resort fallbacks when the env vars aren't loaded (e.g. one-off CLI scripts that bypass Settings). default_temperature stays JSON-resident since it has no env override yet.

vision._note: Native image input is emitted only when enabled is true; unknown/absent providers get a text placeholder instead (a rejected image block would poison journaled history). Read by services/llm/media.py provider_supports_vision. False here until the OpenAI request encoder renders image blocks (Responses input_image in function_call_output; Chat Completions hoist-to-user-turn) — flipping it early would hydrate bytes the encoder silently drops. Anthropic ships the first encoder; text-only providers keep the visionAnalyze delegate tool.

openai._models_note: GPT-6 Astra (+ -pro) appear in the 2026-09-11 registry refresh ($10/$50 per MTok, 1.05M context, 128K max output, effort thinking) and are curated as the top tier; the default stays gpt-5.6-sol ($4/$20 per developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing on 2026-09-15 — terra $2/$12, luna $0.20/$1.20; the router cache under-reports sol at $2/$10), the same price-over-flagship call as anthropic keeping claude-opus-5 over claude-fable-5-1. The rolling -latest aliases (gpt-astra-latest, gpt-sol-latest, gpt-terra-latest, gpt-luna-latest) and the gpt-5.6 alias for Sol are deliberately not curated: real model names only, like gemini. GPT-5.6 family (sol/terra/luna) GA 2026-07-09. gpt-5.5 / gpt-5.4 remain GA as legacy tiers. Dropped: gpt-5.2 (new requests blocked 2026-06-30), o3 (API shutdown 2026-12-11), o4-mini (API shutdown 2026-10-23) — they fall back to _default constraints if still selected before shutdown.

bedrock._models_note: Bedrock model ids are INFERENCE PROFILE ids, not foundation-model ids: every current Claude model is INFERENCE_PROFILE-only, so us.anthropic.claude-opus-5 invokes and the bare anthropic.claude-opus-5 is rejected as a validation error. The us. prefix routes within the United States; global.anthropic.* twins exist for every entry above (eu. / apac. exist in those regions). Model access is enabled once per account in the Bedrock console before any id here resolves.
bedrock._detection_note: Deliberately narrower than anthropic's ["claude", "anthropic"], and ordered before it: detect_provider_from_model returns the first substring hit in file order, so a profile id classifies as bedrock while a bare claude-sonnet-4-6 still classifies as anthropic.
bedrock._region_note: Lowest-precedence region default. AWS_REGION, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, in the server environment override it (see BedrockProvider.resolve_region — the Anthropic SDK itself reads only the former). The region must be one where the account has model access; a profile enabled elsewhere is a 404 here.
bedrock._token_map_note: Keyed by full profile prefix because ModelRegistry prefix-matches with startswith(); a bare "claude-opus-5" key would never match "us.anthropic.claude-opus-5". Both cross-region prefixes are listed for that reason.
bedrock._capability_note: These two lists mirror anthropic's and are matched by substring (AnthropicProvider._model_policy uses `prefix in model`), so the bare family names match the profile-prefixed ids. Server-side context compaction is deliberately absent and is dropped by BedrockProvider.chat: the compact-2026-01-12 beta is first-party-only and 400s on bedrock-runtime.

anthropic._models_note: claude-opus-5 (released 2026-07-24) is the Opus flagship and default: near-Fable intelligence at Opus pricing ($5/$25), 1M context, 128K max output. claude-fable-5-1 (registry 2026-09-03: $10/$50, 1M context, 128K max output) is the most capable generally available model (platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview on 2026-09-15: cache reads are 2.5% of input on 5.1 versus 10% elsewhere; claude-sonnet-5 is $2/$10) and supersedes claude-fable-5, which stays curated as the same-priced prior tier. The adaptive-thinking / sampling-removed lists below match by prefix, so the existing claude-fable-5 entries cover 5.1. The claude-opus-5-fast variant (2x pricing) is deliberately not curated here; select it via the live dropdown if needed.
anthropic._capability_note: Two request-shape breaks landed together in the Claude 4.7+ generations: `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` are rejected (400 `temperature is deprecated for this model`), and the `{type: enabled, budget_tokens: N}` thinking form is rejected in favour of `{type: adaptive}`. Both lists are prefix-matched by AnthropicProvider._model_policy. claude-opus-4-6 / claude-sonnet-4-6 are deliberately absent: adaptive is recommended there but budget_tokens still works, so they keep the legacy shape until Anthropic removes it.

gemini._detection_patterns_note: 'gemma' makes is_model_valid_for_provider accept the API-served Gemma models (gemma-4-*-it) on gemini nodes — without it the four agent-path call sites silently swap gemma to default_model. Cerebras keeps its own 'gemma-4' pattern for its gemma-4-31b (no -it suffix); is_model_valid_for_provider is per-provider so both coexist. Only the runtime-unused detect_provider_from_model classifier prefers gemini for gemma-* names (dict order).

vision._note: See openai.vision._note — off until the Gemini encoder renders inline_data parts beside function_response.

gemini._models_note: Real (concrete) model names only — no -latest rolling aliases. The curated list (max_output_tokens keys) serves BOTH the Gemini Developer API (AIza keys) and Vertex / Agent Platform (AQ. keys); gemini-* entries live-verified on both endpoints (2026-06-12). Vertex 404s on -latest aliases and its models.list rejects API keys, which is why the dropdown is curated instead of live-fetched. Gemma exception: gemma-4-31b-it + gemma-4-26b-a4b-it are served ONLY on the Developer API (free tier, ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/core/gemma_on_gemini_api, verified 2026-07-11) — Vertex keys must not see them, hence vertex_incompatible_models below. Gemma 4 supports systemInstruction and function calling natively (unlike the gemma-3 era); max output is undocumented, so the curated 8192 is a conservative fallback (registry cache wins when present).
gemini._vertex_incompatible_models_note: Curated models that only exist on the Gemini Developer API, filtered out of fetch_models when the key is a Vertex / Agent Platform key (GeminiProvider._vertex). Gemma is Model Garden self-deploy on Vertex (the 26B MaaS variant needs a different '-maas' id on a different surface), so the plain ids 404 there.
gemini._new_models_note: gemini-3.8-flash (default) is stable on the Gemini API per ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.8-flash (2026-09-15: 1,048,576 in / 65,536 out, thinking levels low/medium/high, minimal rejected); gemini-3.7-flash shares the shape. 3.6/3.7/3.8 Flash are $0.75/$3.75 until 2027-01-01, then $1.50/$7.50 (Gemini pricing page); gemini-3.5-flash is $1.50/$9.00, Flash-Lite $0.30/$2.50. The 3.7/3.8 entries are NOT yet live-verified against Vertex / Agent Platform keys like the older entries — drop them into vertex_incompatible_models if a Vertex 404 shows up. gemini-3.8-live and the transcribe / TTS / image models are different endpoints and stay out of the chat list. gemini-3.5-pro is still not GA on the public API (enterprise Vertex preview only) so it stays out of the curated list.
gemini._incompatible_models_note: Models that the dropdown should hide because they need a different API endpoint than `generate_content`. antigravity-preview-05-2026 requires the Interactions API; selecting it currently surfaces a `google.genai.errors.APIError`. ChatUnifier reads this list in fetch_models and filters before returning. Drop entries here when the unifier gains routing support for the alternate endpoint.

groq._popular_note: Empty per the 1M-context policy — no Groq-served model reaches 1M (all top out at 131072). Models remain reachable via live fetch_models.
groq._open_world_note: Groq serves owner-qualified ids (openai/gpt-oss-120b) that contain no 'groq', so a pattern check would swap a valid selection for default_model.
groq._models_note: Default moved to openai/gpt-oss-120b (production route). console.groq.com/docs/models on 2026-09-15 lists the production text models as llama-3.1-8b-instant, llama-3.3-70b-versatile and the two GPT-OSS sizes (Groq had announced the Llama deprecations on 2026-06-17; they are still served). qwen/qwen3-32b is gone; the preview text models are qwen/qwen3.8-27b (131072 context, 16384 max completion) and minimaxai/minimax-m2.7 (196608 / 131072), curated with those documented caps.

cerebras._popular_note: Empty per the 1M-context policy — no Cerebras model reaches 1M (all 131072). Models remain reachable via live fetch_models.
cerebras._models_note: Per inference-docs.cerebras.ai/models/overview on 2026-09-15 the public endpoints serve exactly two models: gpt-oss-120b (65K free / 131K paid context) and qwen-3.8-27b (64K free / 128K paid). zai-glm-4.7 and gemma-4-31b are no longer listed and were dropped from the curated maps (the zai-glm / gemma-4 detection patterns stay so an old node parameter is still recognised rather than silently swapped); other families exist only on Dedicated Endpoints. Max completion is undocumented for qwen-3.8-27b; the curated 40960 mirrors gpt-oss-120b and the registry cache wins when present. qwen-3-235b* variants are shut down.
cerebras._thinking_note: Empty since zai-glm-4.7 left the public endpoints: Cerebras documents no thinking control for gpt-oss-120b or qwen-3.8-27b, so nothing is sent.

xai._popular_note: grok-4.6 (registry 2026-09-03, 500K context, $2/$6), grok-4.5 (released 2026-07-08) and grok-3 excluded per the 1M-context policy (500K / 500K / 131072); reachable via live fetch_models. Default stays grok-4.20 (1M) so the default is selectable from the global list.
xai._models_note: grok-4.20 is documented at 1,000,000 context on docs.x.ai/docs/models/grok-4.20 (2026-09-15; the router cache says 2M, the vendor number wins) at $1.25/$2.50, tiered to $2.50/$5.00 once the prompt passes 200K tokens; the bare grok-4.20 id is accepted alongside the dated grok-4.20-0309-reasoning ids and grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309. grok-4.6 and grok-4.5: 500K context, reasoning effort low/medium/high/xhigh (default high), $2/$6 tiered to $4/$12. Output cap undocumented by xAI — curated 131072 matches the rest of the grok family; registry cache wins when present.

deepseek._popular_note: All three curated ids are 1M-context; deepseek-v4-flash stays in the maps only as the retired alias DeepSeek still accepts.
deepseek._models_note: Per api-docs.deepseek.com (updates + pricing, 2026-09-15): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash shipped 2026-09-10 as deepseek-flash (native multimodal, 1M context, 384K max output, $0.15/$0.60 per MTok off-peak, cache hit $0.003; peak hours 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Mon-Fri double it). deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are retired names that still resolve to V4.1-Flash at the Flash price, so the default moved to deepseek-flash. deepseek-v4-pro (GA 2026-08-13, kept past 2026-09-14) is 1M / 384K at $0.66/$1.98 off-peak. deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner were discontinued three months after the 2026-04-24 V4 launch and are no longer curated. Dated snapshots (-0731 / -0813) and the -latest aliases are deliberately not curated.

kimi._popular_note: Only kimi-k3 meets the 1M-context policy (k2.x are 262144); k2.x remain reachable via live fetch_models.
kimi._models_note: kimi-k3 GA (platform.kimi.ai): 2.8T params, 1M context, vision + tool calling + structured outputs, $3/$15 per MTok ($0.30 cache-hit). Default max_completion_tokens 131072 (configurable up to the full window). platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat (2026-09-15) lists kimi-k2.7-code ($0.95/$4.00, cache hit $0.19), kimi-k2.7-code-highspeed ($1.90/$8.00) and kimi-k2.6 ($0.95/$4.00, cache hit $0.16) as the remaining k2 tiers; kimi-k2.5 is no longer listed and was dropped from the curated maps.

mistral._popular_note: Empty per the 1M-context policy — Mistral tops out at 262144 (large/medium/small). Models remain reachable via live fetch_models.
mistral._models_note: The -latest aliases resolve (docs.mistral.ai models overview, 2026-09-15) to mistral-medium-3504 (Medium 3.5, 256K), mistral-small-2603 (Small 4, 256K, $0.15/$0.60), mistral-large-2512 (Large 3, 256K, $0.50/$1.50) and codestral-2508 ($0.30/$0.90). Mistral does not publish max-output caps; the curated values are conservative and the registry cache wins when present.

sarvam._popular_note: Empty per the 1M-context policy — sarvam-105b tops out at 131072. Both models stay reachable via the per-node dropdown (fetch_models returns the curated list) and via the global selector, which falls back to the max_output_tokens keys when popular_models is empty.
sarvam._models_note: sarvam-105b (128K ctx) and sarvam-30b (64K ctx), OpenAI-compatible at api.sarvam.ai/v1. sarvam-m is deprecated/removed and deliberately absent. docs.sarvam.ai (2026-09-15) also lists sarvam-105b-conversations (32K) and beta third-party routes (Gemma-4 31B, GLM 5.2 / 5.3 / 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Flash) on the pricing page without documenting their API ids, so they are not curated. Reasoning is ON by default (reasoning_effort defaults to 'medium' server-side) and the trace comes back as message.reasoning_content, which OpenAIProvider._normalize already reads.
sarvam._models_listing_note: Sarvam ships NO model-list endpoint — verified against https://docs.sarvam.ai/openapi.json (25 paths, none for model listing). OpenAIProvider.fetch_models reads this flag and swaps models.list() for a 1-token chat probe plus the curated list. Without it the 404 becomes an openai.OpenAIError, ChatUnifier turns that into NodeUserError, and AIService.fetch_models re-raises before its curated fallback — breaking both credential validation and the model dropdown.
sarvam._max_output_note: SUBSCRIPTION-TIER CAP, not a model limit — this is the one provider here whose output ceiling depends on the ACCOUNT rather than the model. Sarvam documents Starter 4096 / Pro 16384 / Business 128000 for sarvam-105b and 4096 / 8192 / 64000 for sarvam-30b, and rejects anything above your tier with a 400 ('max_tokens (N) exceeds the maximum allowed ... for your subscription tier'). services/llm/config.py::resolve_max_tokens uses this number BOTH as the default budget when a node leaves max_tokens unset AND as the ceiling it clamps larger user values down to, so a single value has to hold for every account — hence the Starter cap, the only figure that succeeds on all tiers. Sarvam's own API default is 2048, so 4096 is already generous. ON PRO OR BUSINESS: raise these to your tier's ceiling (setting max_tokens on the node alone is NOT enough — resolve_max_tokens clamps it back down to whatever is written here). Do not use the Business figures as a default: they are ~98% of each context window, leaving no room for a prompt.
sarvam._thinking_note: reasoning_models is deliberately empty: listing sarvam there would set temperature_allowed=False and pin temperature to 1.0, but Sarvam accepts temperature alongside reasoning. thinking_default_on is deliberately absent too — it emits Moonshot's proprietary extra_body.thinking={'type':'disabled'}, which Sarvam never documented. With both omitted, thinking off = Sarvam's own default (reasoning on, effort medium) and thinking on = our reasoning_effort.

ollama._description: Local Ollama server (OpenAI-compatible /v1). No `default_model` because the dropdown should reflect the user's actually-pulled models — fetch_models hits the user's saved {provider}_proxy URL and returns whatever Ollama reports; when the server is offline we want an empty list (a 'start your server' cue), not a placeholder name the user almost certainly doesn't have.

auth._note: Ollama's OpenAI-compatibility docs (docs.ollama.com/openai): api_key='ollama', 'required but ignored'. Read by services/llm/config.py::resolve_credential.

lmstudio._description: Local LM Studio server (pure OpenAI-compatible). Same no-default-model rule as ollama — the dropdown reflects what the user has loaded in LM Studio, not a fake placeholder.

auth._note: LM Studio's OpenAI-compatibility docs use api_key='lm-studio'; the server needs no key unless API tokens are enabled. Read by services/llm/config.py::resolve_credential.

openai_compatible._description: User-named OpenAI-compatible endpoints: llama.cpp, vLLM, a LiteLLM proxy, a second Ollama host, and so on. No base_url and no default_model: each endpoint is its own provider reference, openai_compatible:<slug>, whose resolved base URL and model list are stored on its credential rows when it is saved (RFC-0003 D13). This block supplies the fallbacks every endpoint shares.

auth._note: Sent when an endpoint has no key: the value llama.cpp's server README uses in its OpenAI client example. Servers without auth ignore it, and the OpenAI SDK refuses an empty key.

openai_compatible._limits_note: Deliberately conservative. An overestimate overflows the server (or, on Ollama, silently truncates the prompt); an underestimate only compacts early. Saving an endpoint replaces these per model when the server reports its real context (llama.cpp /props, vLLM max_model_len) or the LiteLLM table knows the model id.
